steps.title: Install Tailscale on both servers
steps.where: application server (VPS ov-ab27bf, user devops) and monitoring server (office VM n8nserver, user devops01)
steps.goal: Create a private, encrypted network between the cloud server and the office server, so monitoring data never travels on the open internet and no port has to be opened to the internet.

commands.explain: Downloads and runs Tailscale's official installer: it adds Tailscale's apt repository and installs the tailscale package and the tailscaled service.
Joins this machine to your tailnet. It prints a login link: open it, sign in with the company account, approve the machine. The machine then gets a fixed private address in 100.64.0.0/10.
Shows the machine's Tailscale address: 100.69.47.69 for the VPS (name 'vps'), 100.118.61.101 for n8nserver (name 'local-vm').

verify.expect: Both machines are listed, the other one is not 'offline'.
pong from local-vm ... via <direct path or DERP>

steps.notes: Tailscale uses WireGuard. Traffic goes directly between the two machines (UDP 41641) or through Tailscale's relays, always encrypted end to end.

steps.phase: B. Storage on the monitoring server
steps.title: Loki: the logs database (port 3100)
steps.where: monitoring server (office VM n8nserver, user devops01)
steps.goal: Receive and store every log line sent by Alloy (application, database, website, system) and answer LogQL queries for Grafana.

commands.cmd: sudo apt-get install -y loki   # from the Grafana apt repository
commands.explain: Installs Loki as the 'loki' systemd service with its configuration in /etc/loki/config.yml.
Single-node configuration: storage on the local disk, HTTP port 3100, and the limits we set later (step D3).
Starts Loki now and at every boot.

steps.notes: The exact way Loki was installed is recorded by scripts/collect-monitoring.sh (state/monitoring/loki-unit.txt).

steps.phase: B. Storage on the monitoring server
steps.title: Prometheus in Docker: the metrics database (port 9091)
steps.where: monitoring server (office VM n8nserver, user devops01)
steps.goal: Store the measurements (CPU, memory, disk, network, database, programs) that Alloy pushes every 15 seconds.

commands.cmd:
docker run -d --name vps_prometheus --restart unless-stopped -p 9091:9090 \
  -v /path/to/prometheus.yml:/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml:ro -v vps_prom_data:/prometheus \
  prom/prometheus --config.file=/etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml --storage.tsdb.path=/prometheus --web.enable-remote-write-receiver
commands.explain: Runs Prometheus in a container named vps_prometheus. Port 9091 of the server goes to port 9090 of the container. --web.enable-remote-write-receiver lets Alloy PUSH metrics to /api/v1/write (Prometheus normally pulls). The data lives in a Docker volume, so recreating the container keeps the history.

files: monitoring/prometheus/container.env (exact image, ports, volumes, arguments from docker inspect)
steps.notes: A port published by Docker is reachable even if ufw does not allow it (Docker writes its own firewall rules). See docs/06-improvements.md.

steps.phase: C. Collection on the application server
steps.title: Install Grafana Alloy
steps.goal: One agent that reads the logs and measures the server, then sends everything to the office through Tailscale.

commands.cmd:
sudo mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
wget -q -O - https://apt.grafana.com/gpg.key | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.gpg >/dev/null
echo 'deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/grafana.gpg] https://apt.grafana.com stable main' | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/grafana.list
commands.explain: Adds Grafana's signed apt repository (the key proves the packages really come from Grafana).

commands.cmd: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y alloy
commands.explain: Installs Alloy: service 'alloy', configuration /etc/alloy/config.alloy, settings /etc/default/alloy, local web UI on 127.0.0.1:12345.

steps.phase: C. Collection on the application server
steps.title: Let Alloy read the logs
steps.goal: Alloy runs as the unprivileged user 'alloy'; it needs read access to the log files and the system journal.

commands.explain: Group adm can read /var/log/nginx and /var/log/postgresql; group systemd-journal can read the journal.
Checks that the application log file is readable by Alloy (path as written in config.alloy).
A new group membership is only seen by a restarted process.

steps.phase: C. Collection on the application server
steps.title: PostgreSQL role for statistics only
steps.goal: Let Alloy read PostgreSQL's statistics (connections, cache, locks, size) without any access to the application data.

commands.cmd: sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE ROLE alloy_monitor LOGIN PASSWORD '...';" -c "GRANT pg_monitor TO alloy_monitor;"
commands.explain: pg_monitor is a built-in PostgreSQL role that can read statistics views only.

steps.phase: C. Collection on the application server
steps.title: Alloy configuration: logs and metrics
steps.goal: Describe, block by block, what Alloy reads and where it sends it. Full explanation of every block: docs/03-alloy-explained.md.

commands.explain: Logs: application (multi-line, level and logger extracted), PostgreSQL, Nginx (HTTP status extracted), systemd journal -> loki.write to http://100.118.61.101:3100. Metrics: server (unix exporter), programs (process exporter), PostgreSQL (postgres exporter), availability probes (blackbox), Alloy itself -> prometheus.remote_write to http://100.118.61.101:9091.
Checks the syntax before restarting (a typo would stop the whole collection).
Loads the new configuration.

verify.cmd: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:12345/api/v0/web/components | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print({c["health"]["state"] for c in json.load(sys.stdin)})'

steps.notes: We added the blocks with a small Python script that replaces each block by its name (safe to run twice). The repository now holds the whole file.

steps.title: Fixes made along the way
steps.where: monitoring server (office VM n8nserver, user devops01)
steps.goal: Problems we met and how we solved them.

commands.explain: In the Loki configuration: very long application log lines (tracebacks) were rejected; now they are kept, cut at 256 KB.
The 'prometheus-2' data source pointed to a wrong address: CPU, memory and disk panels showed 'No data'.
The PostgreSQL error panels used a 'level' label that PostgreSQL logs do not have: replaced by a text filter.

steps.title: http://dashboard.local on the office network
steps.where: monitoring server (office VM n8nserver, user devops01)
steps.goal: An easy address that works from any computer or phone of the office network, and nowhere else.

commands.cmd: sudo apt-get install -y nginx avahi-daemon avahi-utils
commands.explain: Nginx = web server in front of Grafana; Avahi = announces names on the local network (mDNS, the '.local' names).
Nginx answers on port 80 for the name dashboard.local and forwards to Grafana (including websockets for live updates).
A small service that keeps announcing 'dashboard.local = 192.168.15.14' on the office network.

commands.cmd:
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.15.0/24 to any port 80 proto tcp
sudo ufw allow from 192.168.15.0/24 to any port 5353 proto udp
commands.explain: Port 80 and the mDNS announcements, for the office network only. Missing port 80 rule = the 'timed out' error we saw.

verify.expect: 200 or 302 (a 502 means Nginx cannot reach Grafana: wrong upstream address, which we fixed)

steps.title: Mail relay (Postfix) on the VPS
steps.goal: Send the alert emails directly to the recipients' mail servers, without any external SMTP account.

commands.explain: Checks that the hosting provider does not block outgoing port 25 (needed to deliver mail directly).
Installs Postfix without questions ('Internet Site' preset).
Listens only on localhost and the Tailscale address; relays only for n8nserver; every alert leaves with one sender address (sender_canonical).
Postfix waits for the Tailscale address at boot, and retries if it is not ready.

commands.cmd: sudo ufw allow in on tailscale0 from 100.118.61.101 to any port 25 proto tcp
commands.explain: Only n8nserver can hand mail to this relay.

verify.cmd:
printf 'Subject: test

test
' | sendmail -f alertes@<domain> devops01@brothersbusinessintelligence.com; sudo journalctl -u postfix@- -n 20 | grep status=

steps.title: Grafana alert rules and email contact point
steps.where: monitoring server (office VM n8nserver, user devops01)
steps.goal: An email within about a minute when something goes wrong, a reminder every 4 hours, and a 'resolved' email.

commands.explain: Grafana hands its emails to the Postfix relay through Tailscale (private link, no password).

Alerting as code: contact point 'Équipe supervision' (the recipients), the notification policy (group, wait 30 s, repeat 4 h) and 5 rules: application errors, PostgreSQL errors, website 5xx, application silent for 30 min, system service errors.
Grafana reads provisioning files at start.

verify.cmd: Grafana > Alerting > Contact points > Équipe supervision > Test
verify.expect: the test email arrives (check spam the first time)
